title: Whole application
summary: Prepare trusted knowledge ahead of time; retrieve permitted evidence and assemble context at runtime. The model lifecycle and four supporting pillars help coordinate, protect, evaluate, and monitor both flows.
constraint: Establish which layer must change and the hard requirement it must meet; then compare managed support, supported extensions, and any remaining custom work.
managed: Bedrock handles eligible model inference; Knowledge Bases handles supported RAG stages; Step Functions handles explicit durable workflows. Each service manages its configured contract, not the application’s whole business outcome.
extension: If one ingestion step needs domain-specific chunks, use a supported Knowledge Bases Lambda transformation. If context needs business rules, add application assembly/validation around the managed model call.
ownership: The team defines success, access, source freshness, safe action rules, evaluation, and recovery. Implement the unsupported responsibility and test its boundary instead of rebuilding every managed stage.
capability: Bedrock inference, Knowledge Bases Retrieve/RetrieveAndGenerate, Lambda, Step Functions, and IAM/data authorization fit different responsibilities. Choose from the required boundary.
clue: Custom chunking points to ingestion; poor candidate order points to retrieval/reranking; a durable human wait points to workflow state. Service choice follows that diagnosis.
trap: A custom requirement at one stage does not justify rebuilding the whole application.
example: A policy assistant prepares approved documents, answers with permitted passages, and may propose a controlled business action. Each responsibility has a different acceptance test.

title: Requirements
summary: Define the business problem and the outcome the application must produce before selecting a model. Is the task summarization, classification, reasoning over supplied evidence, or proposing a tool action? Establish why a GenAI component fits, and keep exact business rules and action authority in deterministic controls.
questions: What does success mean? Define the expected answer or action, difficult examples, and critical cohorts—not just fluent output.
What must the model work with? Identify input modalities, context size, and whether facts are supplied, private, or frequently changing.
What limits the solution? Record quality, safety, latency, cost, approved data locations, access scope, and any required approval.
decision: Turn these requirements into representative held-out cases. Select then compares model/task fit. Clearer instructions or examples address task/format gaps; RAG supplies required evidence; supported customization is a candidate when stable behavior still fails evaluated prompting. Compare measured benefit and lifecycle cost rather than assuming a larger model is necessary.
constraint: The approach must meet the business outcome and every hard constraint, measured on representative cases rather than inferred from model size.
managed: No AWS service defines your business acceptance criteria. Bedrock supplies eligible model inference; Knowledge Bases supplies supported evidence retrieval. Your evaluation establishes whether those capabilities meet the use case.
extension: Prompt Management can version clearer instructions/examples; Knowledge Bases can add current evidence; its Lambda transformation can change supported ingestion behavior. Check that specific extension before commissioning a custom pipeline.
ownership: Define expected answers/actions, critical cohorts, allowed inputs/locations, and measurable quality/cost/latency limits. Enforce business permissions and turn difficult examples into held-out acceptance tests.
capability: Instruction/format gap → Prompt Management plus output validation. Current private-fact gap → Knowledge Bases/RAG. Evaluated stable behavior gap → eligible Bedrock customization or SageMaker adaptation with deployment/evaluation controls.
clue: “Policy changes daily” calls for current evidence. “Labels overlap” calls for explicit task rules/examples. “Stable behavior still fails a clear evaluated prompt” makes supported customization a candidate to test.
trap: Model size and public benchmark rank do not prove workload fit. Identify whether the gap is task definition, evidence, model capability, or stable behavior before changing weights.
example: For an expense-policy assistant, “good” means answering from the current permitted policy, respecting exceptions, meeting response-time/cost limits, and never authorizing an invalid refund.

title: Source
summary: Approved facts, media, and datasets enter here. Establish provenance, versions, permitted use, and update/delete behavior before creating derived copies.
constraint: Identify approved source versions and caller entitlement, and decide how updates/deletes reach every relevant derived copy.
managed: S3 and supported databases store source records; eligible connectors expose them to the downstream path. Storage or connector success does not establish that the records are correct and approved.
extension: Use a supported source connector where it fits; otherwise adapt access/format through a controlled connector or preprocessing step while preserving source/version identity.
ownership: Define source ownership, permission, freshness, provenance, and update/delete handling. Carry those facts into chunks/indexes and verify that a changed source reaches derived copies.
capability: S3 documents, an authoritative database, or a scoped business API supplies the fact. Knowledge Bases source synchronization is a separate downstream responsibility.
clue: “Private manuals change daily” points to current source evidence and synchronization, not memorizing facts in weights.
trap: Changing a source object does not prove the index, cache, or generated answer was refreshed.
example: If the current manual lacks the exception a user asks about, no retrieval setting can supply it. First establish which record/version is authoritative.

title: Preprocess
summary: Convert or validate inputs before creating chunks, embeddings, datasets, or model requests. Preserve meaning rather than merely producing text.
constraint: Prepared output must preserve required meaning, satisfy the downstream schema, and meet sensitive-data policy before derived copies are created.
managed: Textract extracts supported document structure; Transcribe converts supported speech; Glue/Data Quality handles ETL/rules; Comprehend detects supported text spans; Data Automation handles supported media extraction.
extension: Validate and reconstruct relationships around extraction output, apply required redaction, and use explicit fail/quarantine handling when prepared data violates the rule.
ownership: Own domain meaning, record validation, transformations, and checks on the actual downstream bytes. A successful extraction job or quality report does not prove data is safe to index.
capability: Textract for forms/tables; Transcribe when a transcript is required; Data Automation for eligible structured media extraction; Glue/Data Quality for explicit data gates; Comprehend plus applied redaction for supported sensitive text.
clue: “The PDF condition disappeared during extraction” is a parsing/preprocessing problem before retrieval.
trap: Detection is not redaction, and accurate embeddings cannot restore missing extracted text.
example: A scanned table’s amount and exception must stay associated after extraction; a PII detector must be followed by verified redaction before indexing.

comparison.title: Prepare the input: which capability fits?
rows: Supported document / image / audio / video outputs
comparison.note: Choose from the required prepared output. Parsing/chunking cannot recover facts already lost during extraction.

title: Ingestion
summary: Build searchable evidence: Parse → Chunk → Metadata → Embed → Index. This is preparation/synchronization work, not the per-question ranking path.
constraint: Preserve useful evidence boundaries, trusted metadata, vector compatibility, and current searchable records under the selected ingestion contract.
managed: Knowledge Bases coordinates configured supported parsing, chunking, embedding, and indexing into its eligible backing store. Check job completion and failures to prove that evidence became searchable.
extension: A Knowledge Bases Lambda transformation can implement custom chunking or chunk metadata within its input/output contract. Managed embedding/indexing can remain after that supported hook.
ownership: Own the domain-specific hook, source/metadata correctness, and unsupported ingestion gaps. Test actual indexed records and update/delete behavior; a started job is not completed synchronization.
capability: Knowledge Bases ingestion jobs plus supported parser/chunk/embedding/store settings create searchable evidence. Lambda transformation extends ingestion, not query-time ranking.
clue: “Custom chunk boundaries, managed retrieval retained” points to an ingestion extension.
trap: A Lambda ingestion transformation does not control query-time ranking.
example: A manual’s rule, exception, source version, and access scope must survive parsing/chunking and be stored with compatible vectors before a question can retrieve it.

comparison.title: Chunking: which evidence boundary fits?
comparison.note: Check KB type: fully managed KBs currently lack semantic chunking and Lambda ingestion hooks; those rows need an eligible configurable KB path. Custom chunking with the supported Lambda transformation uses NONE before the hook.

title: Knowledge store
summary: Keep searchable chunks, vectors, metadata, and source references. A Knowledge Base coordinates RAG; its vector store holds/searches the indexed evidence.
constraint: The store must support the required index/query/filter contract, scale, synchronization, and permitted access.
managed: The selected store persists/searches eligible text, vectors, and metadata. Knowledge Bases coordinates its supported RAG integration and exposes retrieval/generation APIs for that configuration.
extension: Configure supported fields, metadata filters, and retrieval options. Use separate Retrieve/context orchestration where it meets a requirement the combined path cannot express.
ownership: Own unsupported search policy and any custom indexing/synchronization you take on. Verify the store/Knowledge Base integration before concluding that the whole application needs custom RAG.
capability: Knowledge Bases plus supported OpenSearch/other vector-store integration fits managed RAG. A store by itself provides indexed search rather than an enterprise assistant.
clue: “OpenSearch is the backing store” does not say who owns the rest of RAG.
trap: OpenSearch does not automatically mean custom RAG. A vector database is not an enterprise assistant.
example: OpenSearch can be the backing store of managed Knowledge Bases RAG. Seeing the store name does not tell you who owns ingestion, retrieval, or citations.

comparison.title: RAG manager, retriever, or backing store?
rows: Do not assume Aurora’s contract applies
comparison.note: These are different architecture layers, not mutually exclusive substitutes. Derive access scope from trusted identity. Kendra is in maintenance and closed to new customers; existing-customer/exam scenarios still need its retrieval boundary.

title: User / API
summary: Accept a request with trusted identity, its task, and an appropriate delivery contract. Carry scope and correlation through downstream stages.
constraint: Accept only a valid authorized task under a clear delivery, private-path, and admission contract.
managed: API Gateway handles the selected API integration; Cognito/appropriate federation handles configured authentication. Supported VPC endpoints handles eligible private service access.
extension: Application adapters can validate requests, derive trusted scope, select permitted model routes, and implement token/team admission that generic request throttles cannot express.
ownership: Own business/data entitlement, authoritative state, request/accounting rules, and truthful synchronous/streaming/background status. Client-provided tenant IDs are not sufficient authority.
capability: API Gateway plus appropriate identity and application routing forms the entry path. IAM/backend authorization and scoped retrieval/tool checks establishes permitted work.
clue: “Several teams need common model policy” points to a shared gateway, not just direct invocation.
trap: Authentication identifies the caller; it does not establish document or tool entitlement.
example: A signed-in caller can submit a question, but the backend still needs to determine which tenant documents and business actions that caller may use.

title: Retrieval
summary: Turn a question into permitted candidates, rank them, and select evidence for context. Query → query embedding → vector/lexical/hybrid → candidates → reranker → best context.
constraint: Return enough relevant permitted evidence, rank it appropriately, and preserve its meaning within the context budget.
managed: Knowledge Bases Retrieve returns supported candidate evidence, while RetrieveAndGenerate combines its configured retrieval/generation path. Search/reranking behavior depends on the chosen Knowledge Base/store/API contract.
extension: Compose supported filters, search options, reranking, and context selection around Retrieve when needed. Check the contract of each extension and measure coverage before ordering.
ownership: Own trusted caller scope, unsupported query/ranking policy, and evaluation. Preserve managed ingestion where it fits and do not loosen access to improve apparent recall.
capability: Retrieve for inspecting candidates; supported OpenSearch/vector-store search for lexical/semantic/hybrid fit; Bedrock/Knowledge Bases reranking for existing-candidate order.
clue: Absent candidate → retrieval/earlier evidence boundary. Present but poorly ordered → reranking.
trap: Reranking cannot recover material absent from its candidate input.
example: If the passage is missing from candidates, inspect search/filters; if it is present but ordered badly, evaluate reranking before changing the generator.

comparison.title: Search coverage first; candidate order second
rows: Exact IDs may need keyword/term filters
comparison.note: Candidate absence points upstream; poor ordering points to ranking. Fully managed KBs use hybrid retrieval; configurable search choices depend on the selected KB/store/API.

title: Prompt / context
summary: System instructions + prompt template + user query + retrieved knowledge + conversation context become the model input. Keep untrusted data separate from governing instructions.
constraint: The model input must contain clear governing instructions, the right scoped evidence/history, and a valid task/output contract.
managed: Prompt Management stores supported templates, variables, variants, and versions. Converse or model-specific inference APIs receive the actual messages/context the application supplies.
extension: Add explicit task rules/examples, assemble permitted evidence/history, and use supported output constraints. Check restrictions when invoking a managed prompt with the selected API.
ownership: Own task definitions, authoritative state, scope, rendered payload, semantic validation, and release gates. A saved prompt version does not prove the evaluated version was invoked.
capability: Prompt Management versions reusable instructions; Converse/ConverseStream receives supported context; application/business checks validates facts and actions beyond output shape.
clue: “Right evidence, wrong answer” requires inspecting actual context and task instructions before assuming retrieval is broken.
trap: A versioned prompt, valid JSON, or low temperature does not establish factual truth.
example: A response can follow the JSON schema yet classify a case incorrectly because the prompt never defined how overlapping categories should be handled.

title: Model
summary: Invoke a compatible evaluated model using permitted context. Choose the hosting boundary by required controls, not by whether something is “custom.”
constraint: Invoke a compatible evaluated model within quality, approved-processing, latency/capacity, and serving-control requirements.
managed: Bedrock manages eligible FM inference infrastructure. SageMaker AI provides managed ML jobs/endpoints with deeper choices of model, container, instance, and lifecycle configuration.
extension: Use eligible Bedrock customization/import where it meets the supported contract. Use compatible SageMaker model/container/endpoint configurations when the required control is decisive.
ownership: Own model/task comparison, required serving implementation, capacity sizing, deployment compatibility, and business validation. Accept the operations responsibility associated with the controls you choose.
capability: Bedrock for eligible managed FM-centric inference/customization; SageMaker AI for required ML/hosting control. Verify the exact model, feature, Region, and deployment contract.
clue: “Choose GPU family and serving container” points to hosting control. “Fine-tuned model” alone does not.
trap: Custom does not automatically mean SageMaker. Bedrock also supports eligible customization.
example: A requirement to choose a GPU instance or serving container points to deeper hosting control; a fine-tuned artifact alone does not establish that need.

title: Response
summary: Deliver and validate the result under the caller’s contract. An answer, source citation, tool outcome, and durable job completion are different artifacts.
constraint: The delivered result must satisfy format, meaning, timing, and truthful task-completion requirements.
managed: Bedrock supported synchronous/streaming calls and eligible batch jobs supply model-operation contracts. These do not automatically provide every application transport or business completion check.
extension: Forward streaming events through a supported end-to-end transport, or compose durable asynchronous workers/state and completion notification where the caller need not wait.
ownership: Own disconnects, buffering, partial failure, job reconciliation, citations/meaning checks, and authoritative business status. Return acceptance as pending rather than claiming completion.
capability: Converse/ConverseStream or supported model APIs for bounded/incremental answers; eligible batch for an offline dataset; queues/workflows plus state for durable background work.
clue: Earlier tokens while the user waits → streaming. Caller can leave → async; offline dataset → eligible batch.
trap: Streaming is not asynchronous. A job acknowledgment is not completed business work.
example: Earlier tokens while the caller waits calls for streaming; a job ID with later persisted results calls for background completion. Neither alone proves the business action succeeded.

comparison.title: Choose the caller’s completion contract
comparison.note: Model output, citation, tool result, and durable business completion are different artifacts. Verify the authoritative outcome before claiming success.

title: Model lifecycle
summary: Requirements → representative data → Select → optional Customize/train → Evaluate + approve → Deploy/invoke → Monitor → revisit selection or customization. This changes the model configuration used at runtime; it is not repeated for each request. Prompt engineering and RAG change runtime instructions/evidence rather than model weights.
constraint: Release only the compatible configuration that passed independent requirements, then monitor outcomes and revisit selection/customization when evidence warrants it.
managed: Bedrock provides eligible model/customization/evaluation/inference operations. SageMaker provides managed jobs, pipelines, registry, and endpoint/adapter serving under their supported contracts.
extension: Connect those operations with versioned datasets, automated/domain evaluation, required human approval, attributed live smoke checks, and a compatible rollback route.
ownership: Own the acceptance criteria, artifact/configuration pairing, release authority, critical-cohort gates, and production response. Approval metadata does not deploy a candidate.
capability: Supported Bedrock/SageMaker operations executes the model lifecycle; Registry records eligible versions/approval; delivery orchestration performs explicit promotion and rollback.
clue: Compare the selected or customized model against a held-out baseline; use monitoring evidence to revisit selection or customization.
trap: A trained model or registered artifact is not proof of a safe, deployed, working release.
example: A weekly model/adapter release should bind evaluated data, artifact, prompt/settings, approval, live identity, and rollback rather than simply registering a new version.

title: Orchestration
summary: Choose who controls progress across either data or runtime work: bounded code, explicit states, decoupled events, or model-selected actions.
constraint: Choose the component from who determines the next step and the required duration, state, waits, coupling, and recovery.
managed: Lambda runs bounded tasks; Step Functions persists configured workflow states; EventBridge routes events; SQS buffers work. An eligible agent harness/framework controls model-selected tool loops.
extension: Compose bounded Bedrock/tool tasks inside known workflows, or pass a validated agent proposal to a durable approval/action path. Use a compatible persistent runtime only when required.
ownership: Own tool descriptions and scope, business preconditions, iteration/time/token bounds, retries, idempotency, and rate control. Hosting or orchestration does not grant business permission.
capability: Lambda → bounded code. Step Functions → explicit durable transitions/waits. Agent → observation-driven tool choice. EventBridge/SQS → decoupled routing/buffering. AgentCore Runtime hosts agents; its managed harness can supply a loop.
clue: Known durable sequence + wait/approval → Step Functions. Model chooses next tool from observations → agent.
trap: An agent framework does not replace durable workflow state or business authorization.
example: A model can diagnose which permitted tool to try, then a deterministic workflow can validate the proposal, wait for approval, and perform an idempotent write.

comparison.title: Who decides what happens next?
rows: External session state alone ≠ container need
comparison.note: Compose these responsibilities when needed: agent proposes; backend validates; workflow approves; worker executes. AgentCore Runtime hosts agents; an eligible managed harness supplies the loop.

title: Security / governance
summary: Apply identity, access, isolation, encryption, network, safety, PII, and governance controls at the boundaries they protect—not as one final filter.
constraint: Protect each data/action boundary independently and preserve scope/privacy requirements across source, context, tools, and retained copies.
managed: Cognito/federation, IAM/KMS, supported private endpoints, Guardrails, and discovery/analysis services supply different identity, permission, protection, or content controls.
extension: Add caller-derived retrieval filters, domain authorization, verified redaction, action validation, and supported safety policies at their own boundaries.
ownership: Own tenant-to-record entitlement, transaction policy, bypass removal, approved destinations, and copy-specific retention/deletion. Test denied cases as well as safe-looking output.
capability: IAM/data authorization for access; KMS/TLS for protection; PrivateLink for eligible network paths; Guardrails for supported content risks; Macie/Comprehend for their discovery/text roles.
clue: Tenant A must not retrieve tenant B’s documents → access/filtering before context.
trap: Guardrails is not authorization. Private transport or encryption does not establish entitlement or approved residency.
example: A response filter can block harmful wording while still leaving another tenant’s passage in context. Access must be enforced before that passage is supplied.

comparison.title: Match the control to the protected boundary
rows: LF filters do not block direct S3 bypass
Permission ceiling does not grant access
comparison.note: Controls apply across source, index, request, tool, and log copies. Enforce access before evidence enters context; verify retention/deletion separately.

title: Evaluation / diagnosis
summary: Measure evidence coverage, answer/task quality, safety, latency, and cost before releases and during operation. Diagnose backwards using observed boundary evidence.
constraint: Identify which quality or outcome failed, in which cohort, and at which responsibility before selecting a remedy.
managed: Supported Bedrock model/RAG evaluation provides eligible automated, judge, and human approaches. CloudWatch and traces record operational evidence rather than automatically defining semantic quality.
extension: Add explicit rubrics, expert labels, deterministic fact/business assertions, tool-outcome checks, and independent cohort comparisons to the supported evaluation path.
ownership: Own reference quality, held-out independence, judge calibration, critical acceptance criteria, approval, and rollback policy. Evaluate source support and task completion separately from formatting.
capability: Bedrock evaluation plus appropriate assertions/domain experts measures quality; Retrieve inspects evidence; workflow/tool traces establishes actions; CloudWatch measures emitted operational signals.
clue: Missing evidence, noisy retrieval, and unsupported generated claims are different defects.
trap: High average quality, a real citation, or low latency can hide a critical cohort or unsafe side effect.
example: An average score may rise while one critical cohort regresses. The release gate must inspect that subgroup and actual tool outcomes before promotion.

comparison.title: Which quality boundary failed?
rows: How much retrieved material is useful?
Are claims supported by supplied evidence?
How fast/expensive is a successful task?
comparison.note: Use deterministic checks for objective contracts, calibrated judges for semantic scale, and humans for high-risk nuance. Block a critical-cohort regression even when averages improve.

title: Observability
summary: Collect the evidence needed for the question: trends, caller activity, interaction content, or time across request stages.
constraint: Collect the right evidence for the question while limiting sensitive retention and linking it to the request/version/caller.
managed: CloudWatch records supported metrics/logs; CloudTrail records covered AWS API activity; invocation logging captures supported model content when enabled; instrumented spans records application stages.
extension: Add safe correlation IDs, version/cohort attribution, missing spans, tool/workflow events, and custom outcome metrics. Enable content capture only under the required privacy policy.
ownership: Own instrumentation gaps, sanitized-content policy, event coverage, destination access/encryption/retention, and delivery monitoring. A tracing switch cannot expose every hidden/uninstrumented stage.
capability: CloudTrail → caller/API audit; invocation logging → protected prompt/response evidence; CloudWatch → emitted trends; X-Ray/OTel → instrumented hops; agent/tool traces → observed actions.
clue: Who called → CloudTrail. Prompt/response → invocation logging. Trend → metrics. Slow stage → spans.
trap: Enabling Lambda tracing does not expose every uninstrumented SDK hop or hidden model internal.
example: A total request duration cannot show whether queue wait, retrieval, generation, or a buffering hop caused the delay. Correlate evidence at those boundaries.

comparison.title: Which kind of evidence do you need?
rows: Hidden internals are not automatically visible
comparison.note: Protect scope, sensitive content, destinations, and retention. Correlate evidence with request, data, prompt, model/adapter, and release identity.

title: Documents / images
summary: S3 manuals, PDFs, scans, and images need source/version identity and a supported parsing or native multimodal path.
clue: Tables and scanned conditions must survive extraction.
trap: A readable text file can still omit a material column or exception.
example: A PDF manual needs its rule and table exception preserved together, with the source/version retained for later citation.
managed: S3 stores the approved object; eligible Knowledge Bases parsing ingests supported content.
extension: Use supported parsing or Textract/Data Automation preprocessing when the source structure requires it.
ownership: Validate extracted relationships, source versions, access scope, and update/delete handling before indexing.
capability: S3 for source identity; supported parsing/Textract for extraction; Knowledge Bases for the downstream supported RAG path.
constraint: Preserve the document’s meaning, provenance, permitted use, and supported input format.

title: Databases / business records
summary: Query current authoritative records through an authorized supported connector or business API.
clue: Refund status is a live transaction fact, not a generic prompt example.
trap: A correct source connection is not permission for every caller to every row.
example: A refund answer needs the current authoritative account balance, not a stale natural-language summary of last week’s record.
managed: The supported database or business API stores/serves the authoritative record under its configured access contract.
extension: Use an eligible connector or scoped business tool; normalize only what the downstream task requires.
ownership: Enforce caller-to-record entitlement, freshness, schema checks, and authoritative action outcomes.
capability: Authorized database access or business API for live records; supported retrieval connectors where their contract fits.
constraint: The record must be current and permitted for the caller, with its business meaning preserved.

title: Audio / media
summary: Use supported native modalities or prepare transcripts/structured output for the chosen downstream path.
clue: Choose the representation the selected model and retrieval path actually support.
trap: Transcription is not compulsory for every supported audio-capable model.
example: A recorded conversation contains a condition stated by one speaker; dropping that turn can change the answer’s meaning.
managed: Transcribe supplies supported transcription; eligible native multimodal models or Data Automation handle their supported media tasks.
extension: Prepare a transcript/structured output only when the downstream path requires it, preserving turns and identifiers.
ownership: Validate the relevant spoken facts and permissions; speaker labels alone do not establish verified business roles.
capability: Native supported audio input, Transcribe, or Data Automation according to the required downstream task.
constraint: Preserve the relevant audio meaning and satisfy the model/pipeline’s modality and privacy contract.

title: Documents / tables → Textract
summary: Extract supported text, forms, and tables; reconstruct and validate relationships against the source.
clue: Condition missing from extracted table → repair extraction before re-indexing.
trap: Larger embeddings or chunks cannot restore a condition never extracted.
capability: Textract for supported document extraction; application/Glue checks for the required field relationships and downstream gate.
example: A form’s refund amount and eligibility field must still refer to the same record after extraction.
managed: Textract extracts supported text, forms, and tables; source validation remains separate.
extension: Reconstruct required layout/field relationships and add schema/domain validation around extraction output.
ownership: Check against the source, quarantine invalid records, and preserve version/permission metadata.
constraint: The extracted document must retain the fields, headings, and conditions required to answer correctly.

title: Speech → Transcribe
summary: Prepare supported recordings as text when the downstream pipeline needs transcripts.
clue: Preserve speaker turns and source references when they matter.
trap: Speaker labels do not verify business roles.
capability: Transcribe where text conversion is required; eligible native audio may avoid an unnecessary intermediary.
example: A transcript should retain which turn contains the condition, while the application verifies who actually has business authority.
managed: Transcribe converts supported recordings into transcript output under its configured contract.
extension: Add permitted turn/identifier handling and validation before using the transcript in context or indexing.
ownership: Verify important spoken facts, sensitive-data transformation, and role claims independently of speaker labels.
constraint: Produce a valid permitted transcript only when required and preserve the meaning needed downstream.

title: ETL / quality → Glue
summary: Normalize approved formats, catalog data, and evaluate explicit schema/data rules before creating derived copies.
clue: Invalid dataset records must fail or be quarantined before training/indexing.
trap: A data-quality report is not automatically a deployment or ingestion gate.
capability: Glue/Data Quality for explicit dataset rules/gates; application checks for business semantics not captured by the selected rule.
example: A quality report flags empty records, but the pipeline must explicitly stop or quarantine them before training/indexing.
managed: Glue provides supported ETL/catalogue operations and Data Quality evaluates configured rules.
extension: Configure explicit failure/quarantine/redaction behavior and validate domain-specific fields around ETL output.
ownership: Choose correct rules, preserve meaningful IDs/case, and verify invalid records cannot continue.
constraint: Prepared records must satisfy the actual content/schema rule, not merely produce a quality report.

title: Text / PII → Comprehend
summary: Locate supported entities or sensitive spans; apply and verify required redaction before indexing or logging.
clue: Text-processing PII detection is a different boundary from S3 corpus discovery.
trap: Detection does not itself sanitize every downstream copy.
capability: Comprehend for supported text detection; application transformation plus explicit pipeline gates for verified redaction.
example: A detector locates a personal identifier, but the original text must be transformed before an embedding/log copy is produced.
managed: Comprehend detects supported text entities/sensitive spans; detection itself does not remove them.
extension: Apply supported/domain-appropriate masking or redaction and validate the resulting bytes.
ownership: Own sanitization policy, failure/quarantine handling, and checks across derived copies.
constraint: Sensitive spans must receive the required transformation before unauthorized downstream exposure.

title: Parse
summary: Preserve headings, tables, qualifiers, identifiers, and source versions in the extracted evidence.
clue: The condition is absent before chunking → fix parsing.
trap: Do not diagnose chunking when the original meaning was already lost.
constraint: The actual parser output must preserve the source meaning that chunks will inherit.
example: A row’s price detached from its qualifying column creates misleading text even before chunking starts.
managed: Eligible Knowledge Bases parsers or extraction services supply configured source interpretation.
extension: Use a supported parsing option or preprocess structured content before the managed ingestion path.
ownership: Validate headings, row/cell relationships, qualifiers, identifiers, and source/version lineage.
capability: Knowledge Bases parsing; Textract/Data Automation where their extraction contract fits; source-versus-output validation.

title: Chunking
summary: Create evidence units that balance focused matching, sufficient context, and token budget.
clue: Small matching passage needs surrounding section → evaluate parent/child context.
trap: Semantic or larger chunks are not universally better.
constraint: Evidence units must balance searchable focus, necessary context, and token/storage cost.
example: “Eligible” and “except after activation” should be tested as one meaningful evidence context, not independently useful fragments.
managed: Knowledge Bases applies the supported configured chunking strategy during ingestion.
extension: Choose supported size/overlap, semantic, hierarchical, or a Lambda transformation for required custom boundaries.
ownership: Evaluate representative boundary cases, recall/precision, context cost, and the supported store contract.
capability: Knowledge Bases chunking and supported Lambda transformation changes evidence units before embedding, not runtime ranking.

comparison.title: Chunking: which evidence boundary fits?
comparison.note: Check KB type: fully managed KBs currently lack semantic chunking and Lambda ingestion hooks; those rows need an eligible configurable KB path. Custom chunking with the supported Lambda transformation uses NONE before the hook.

title: Default
summary: Use the service’s default sentence-aware text splitting where representative retrieval tests show it fits.
clue: Start simple when no measured boundary problem requires another strategy.
trap: Default is not proof that table relationships or conditions survived.
capability: Default Knowledge Bases chunking with representative source-to-answer tests.
example: Start with the default split only if tests show that rules and exceptions remain retrievable together.
managed: Knowledge Bases uses its default supported text splitting under the configured ingestion contract.
extension: Compare another supported strategy or custom transformation if boundary cases fail.
ownership: Inspect resulting chunks and retrieval outcomes; the word “default” is not a quality guarantee.
constraint: The default boundaries must preserve sufficient meaning and useful candidate recall for this corpus.

title: Fixed
summary: Choose explicit token size/overlap to control predictable evidence units.
clue: A condition split across boundaries may need overlap or another context strategy.
trap: More overlap increases indexed material; larger chunks can add noise.
capability: Knowledge Bases fixed-size chunking controls predictable units; evaluation determines whether those units fit the documents.
example: A fixed token size with overlap may retain a short rule/exception pair but still split a longer table incorrectly.
managed: Knowledge Bases applies supported fixed-size token/overlap settings.
extension: Adjust supported size/overlap and compare with eligible hierarchical/semantic or custom alternatives.
ownership: Measure retrieval and context cost on boundary cases instead of choosing size by habit.
constraint: Choose supported token/overlap settings that preserve needed context without unnecessary noise.

title: Semantic
summary: Split supported text around meaning/topic changes; evaluate the resulting boundaries and additional cost.
clue: Meaning boundaries may help a corpus with topic transitions.
trap: Semantic chunking does not automatically provide parent substitution.
capability: Knowledge Bases semantic chunking where supported; corpus-specific evaluation rather than a universal “best” strategy.
example: Topic-aware boundaries may help a narrative manual but must still preserve the condition needed by a specific question.
managed: Knowledge Bases provides supported semantic chunking for eligible inputs/configurations.
extension: Compare supported semantic settings and other chunk strategies on identical representative cases.
ownership: Inspect produced boundaries and measure recall, precision, processing cost, and answer support.
constraint: Meaning-based splits must improve this workload enough to justify their processing/context trade-off.

title: Hierarchical
summary: Match child chunks and return broader parent context when the selected store/configuration supports it.
clue: Focused child match needs surrounding section conditions.
trap: Parent context costs tokens and may reduce the returned result count.
capability: Knowledge Bases supported hierarchical parent-child retrieval; GraphRAG has a different contract.
example: A small child passage matches the question; the broader parent supplies its heading and exception to the model.
managed: Supported Knowledge Bases hierarchical chunking/retrieval links matched children to broader parent context.
extension: Choose supported parent/child settings under the selected store contract and compare with other strategies.
ownership: Verify parent substitution, resulting context size, and whether returned evidence still meets count/budget needs.
constraint: The selected configuration must support parent context and preserve relevant evidence within the model budget.

title: Custom
summary: Define domain-specific evidence boundaries when supported built-in strategies do not fit.
clue: Custom chunking does not automatically require custom retrieval.
trap: Check an extension contract before rebuilding ingestion.
extension: Use the supported Lambda transformation for domain-specific chunks or chunk metadata.
example: A legal clause must stay with its own exception and source metadata even when generic token splitting separates them.
managed: Knowledge Bases can keep supported embedding/indexing/retrieval managed after compatible custom ingestion output.
ownership: Own the transformation code, input/output contract, correctness, failures, and representative retrieval tests.
capability: Knowledge Bases Lambda transformation is an ingestion extension; it does not override query-time ranking.
constraint: Implement only the unsupported evidence-boundary requirement while preserving compatible managed stages.

title: Lambda Transformation
summary: A supported Knowledge Bases ingestion hook supplies custom chunks or chunk-level metadata, then returns output for managed processing.
clue: Custom chunking / chunk metadata → supported ingestion extension.
trap: This hook does not own query-time retrieval or reranking.
managed: Knowledge Bases coordinates the supported transformation hook and subsequent configured processing.
extension: Supply compatible Lambda input/output and required intermediate S3 handling for custom chunking/metadata.
ownership: Validate each returned chunk/metadata record, handle errors, and test synchronization and retrieval afterward.
capability: Knowledge Bases custom Lambda transformation plus its documented S3/file contract; Lambda alone is not a custom query ranker.
example: A hook produces clause-sized chunks and source tags, then returns supported references so the Knowledge Base continues ingestion.
constraint: The custom output must satisfy the ingestion contract and preserve chunk meaning, provenance, and trusted scope.

title: Metadata
summary: Attach source/version references, searchable identifiers, and trusted access metadata to evidence.
clue: Tenant filtering and freshness checks depend on reliable metadata.
trap: User-supplied tenant text is not trusted authorization scope.
constraint: Metadata must be complete/correct enough for source identity, freshness, and permitted access.
example: The same passage text with a wrong tenant or version tag can produce an unauthorized or stale answer.
managed: Knowledge Bases/store integration records supported source/chunk metadata and exposes eligible filters.
extension: Use source metadata or a supported transformation to attach required fields; configure supported retrieval filtering.
ownership: Derive access tags from authoritative policy and verify correctness on indexed chunks and query filters.
capability: Knowledge Bases metadata/filters; Lambda transformation for eligible chunk metadata; backend authorization for trusted caller scope.

title: Embedding
summary: Represent documents and queries in a compatible embedding space. Smaller vectors can reduce storage, but require retrieval-quality evaluation.
clue: Document vector and query vector must have matching dimensions and compatible model/configuration.
trap: More dimensions do not guarantee accuracy; matching size alone is not sufficient.
constraint: Document and query vectors must share a compatible model/configuration and meet retrieval-quality requirements.
managed: The selected embedding model produces supported vector representations for the configured pipeline.
extension: Choose supported dimensions/configuration and evaluate alternative embedding models on representative queries.
ownership: Keep document/query embedding spaces compatible and plan re-embedding/index migration when the contract changes.
capability: Titan Text Embeddings V2 or another eligible embedding model with compatible Knowledge Bases/store configuration.
example: Reducing vectors from 1,024 to 512 dimensions may save storage, but the document/query configuration and measured recall must remain acceptable.

title: Titan Text Embeddings V2
summary: Supported vector sizes are 256, 512, and 1,024 dimensions. Compare configurations on the same representative query set.
clue: Keep document/query contracts compatible through an index migration.
trap: Titan G1’s 1,536 dimensions are a different model contract.
capability: Titan Text Embeddings V2 for eligible vector generation; retrieval evaluation determines which supported size fits.
example: Compare 256D, 512D, and 1,024D on the same query set rather than assuming the largest vector always gives the best business answer.
managed: Titan Text Embeddings V2 provides supported 256/512/1,024-dimensional output configurations.
extension: Select a supported size consistently for document and query generation and evaluate the resulting index.
ownership: Measure recall, storage, and latency; version the model/dimension/configuration and migration plan.
constraint: Choose one compatible representation that satisfies measured recall and resource constraints.

title: 256D
summary: 256-dimensional V2 vectors are a supported configuration. Use compatible query vectors and measure recall, storage, and latency.
clue: Choose based on a measured quality target, not vector size alone.
trap: An index accepting the vector does not prove it meets retrieval recall.
example: Document 256D and query 256D are dimension-compatible when the model/configuration is compatible; different dimensions are not.
managed: Titan Text Embeddings V2 can generate supported 256-dimensional vectors.
extension: Configure both ingestion and query generation for that supported representation; compare it with other eligible sizes.
ownership: Verify model/configuration compatibility, index expectations, recall, storage, and latency rather than dimension alone.
capability: Titan V2 256D plus a compatible index/query path; held-out retrieval cases measure the trade-off.
constraint: The 256D document/query configuration must be compatible and preserve required evidence recall.

title: 512D
summary: 512-dimensional V2 vectors are a supported configuration. Use compatible query vectors and measure recall, storage, and latency.
clue: Choose based on a measured quality target, not vector size alone.
trap: An index accepting the vector does not prove it meets retrieval recall.
example: Document 512D and query 512D are dimension-compatible when the model/configuration is compatible; different dimensions are not.
managed: Titan Text Embeddings V2 can generate supported 512-dimensional vectors.
extension: Configure both ingestion and query generation for that supported representation; compare it with other eligible sizes.
ownership: Verify model/configuration compatibility, index expectations, recall, storage, and latency rather than dimension alone.
capability: Titan V2 512D plus a compatible index/query path; held-out retrieval cases measure the trade-off.
constraint: The 512D document/query configuration must be compatible and preserve required evidence recall.

title: 1024D
summary: 1024-dimensional V2 vectors are a supported configuration. Use compatible query vectors and measure recall, storage, and latency.
clue: Choose based on a measured quality target, not vector size alone.
trap: An index accepting the vector does not prove it meets retrieval recall.
example: Document 1024D and query 1024D are dimension-compatible when the model/configuration is compatible; different dimensions are not.
managed: Titan Text Embeddings V2 can generate supported 1024-dimensional vectors.
extension: Configure both ingestion and query generation for that supported representation; compare it with other eligible sizes.
ownership: Verify model/configuration compatibility, index expectations, recall, storage, and latency rather than dimension alone.
capability: Titan V2 1024D plus a compatible index/query path; held-out retrieval cases measure the trade-off.
constraint: The 1024D document/query configuration must be compatible and preserve required evidence recall.

title: Document ↔ query compatibility
summary: Document: 512D ↔ Query: 512D is dimension-compatible. Document: 1024D ↔ Query: 256D is not. Also preserve compatible model/configuration.
clue: A query-only dimension change against the old index breaks the vector contract.
trap: Do not mix embedding spaces just because both vectors have the same length.
example: An index built from 1,024D document vectors cannot be queried as if those records were 256D vectors.
managed: Embedding services produces vectors under a configured model/dimension contract; the store expects compatible indexed/query inputs.
extension: Restore compatible query settings or perform a planned re-embedding/index migration.
ownership: Track both sides of the representation and test recall after a change; matching size does not prove matching embedding space.
capability: Embedding model settings, index configuration, and the query caller together forms the compatibility contract.
constraint: Keep model, dimensions, and applicable configuration compatible for documents and queries.

title: Index / synchronize
summary: Persist chunks, vectors, metadata, and source versions. Check completed updates/deletes and derived copies.
clue: Source changed but old version retrieved → inspect ingestion/index freshness.
trap: S3 modification alone does not prove a successful index update.
constraint: Current permitted evidence must exist in the searchable index with compatible vectors and metadata.
example: An uploaded revised manual is not useful until its current chunk/vector/metadata record is actually searchable and obsolete records are handled.
managed: Knowledge Bases ingestion and the selected supported store performs configured indexing/synchronization.
extension: Use supported ingestion/update handling or implement the unsupported connector/synchronization responsibility explicitly.
ownership: Check completion/failures, exact record/version identity, deletion, and any stale cache/derived copies.
capability: Knowledge Bases ingestion jobs and Retrieve plus store inspection verifies source-to-index-to-candidate completion.

title: Bedrock Knowledge Bases
summary: Managed RAG coordinates supported source ingestion and retrieval with a supported backing store. Retrieve tests evidence separately; RetrieveAndGenerate combines the configured path.
clue: A managed extension can leave the rest of RAG managed.
trap: Knowledge Bases and its vector store are different responsibilities.
example: Custom clause chunking can use a supported Lambda hook while the Knowledge Base retains compatible managed ingestion and retrieval.
managed: Knowledge Bases coordinates the configured supported source, embedding, store, retrieval, and combined answer path.
extension: Use its supported ingestion transformation, metadata/filter, search/reranking, and Retrieve APIs where they fit the required layer.
ownership: Own source/task/access policy and unsupported behavior; verify the chosen Knowledge Base type/store/API feature contract.
capability: Retrieve inspects evidence independently; RetrieveAndGenerate combines configured retrieval/generation; supported extensions can preserve managed responsibilities.
constraint: Confirm required ingestion, store, search, filtering, and citation behavior fits the selected Knowledge Base contract.

title: OpenSearch / vector stores
summary: Store/search indexed vectors, text, and metadata under the selected integration contract.
clue: A managed Knowledge Base can use OpenSearch as its backing store.
trap: Naming OpenSearch does not imply a fully custom RAG pipeline.
capability: OpenSearch or another supported vector store supplies search/storage; Knowledge Bases can own the compatible RAG integration.
example: An OpenSearch vector index can support a managed Knowledge Base; its presence does not require operating the whole RAG pipeline yourself.
managed: The selected store handles configured text/vector/metadata persistence and supported search operations.
extension: Configure eligible fields, indexes, search modes, and filters under the chosen Knowledge Base or custom integration.
ownership: Own unsupported search/synchronization behavior and measure scale, memory, relevance, and permitted access.
constraint: The store/integration must support the required query/filter/index contract and resource scale.

title: Query
summary: Preserve intent, literal identifiers, and trusted scope when forming the retrieval request.
clue: An equipment ID is not interchangeable with semantically similar products.
trap: Normalizing away meaningful identifiers can destroy exact matching.
example: A query about AX-417 must retain the identifier and the authenticated caller’s permitted corpus.
managed: Knowledge Bases or the selected store executes supported retrieval queries/configuration.
extension: Add controlled normalization/decomposition or exact/lexical/hybrid options where the supported path fits.
ownership: Preserve meaning and identifiers, derive scope from trusted identity, and evaluate altered queries without weakening access.
capability: Retrieve/search configuration plus application query preparation targets intent and exact-term requirements.
constraint: Send a faithful, scoped query with the identifiers and filters required for relevant authorized evidence.

title: Query embedding
summary: Generate the query representation compatible with indexed document vectors.
clue: Document/query dimensions and model space must remain compatible.
trap: Changing the query model alone does not migrate the document index.
capability: Titan/eligible embedding model with compatible indexed vectors and retrieval API contract.
example: A new query embedding model cannot silently be compared with document vectors created by an incompatible old model.
managed: The selected embedding service generates query vectors under the configured supported representation.
extension: Keep the document/query settings aligned or migrate/re-embed the document index when needed.
ownership: Verify both configurations and actual index/query inputs; compare recall after the change.
constraint: The query representation must be compatible with indexed document vectors, not merely the same apparent size.

title: Vector / semantic
summary: Find candidates by semantic similarity in a compatible vector space.
clue: Meaning similarity helps paraphrases and concept queries.
trap: Similar text is not proof of exact identifier match or permission.
capability: Supported vector retrieval plus an eligible embedding model addresses semantic intent; exact IDs may need separate lexical signals.
example: “Can I return this?” may match “refund eligibility” semantically even when those exact words differ.
managed: Supported Knowledge Bases/store vector search finds candidates using the configured compatible vector representations.
extension: Choose eligible embedding/search settings and compare with exact/lexical or hybrid signals when the task includes identifiers.
ownership: Evaluate domain/language recall, permitted scope, and thresholds on this dataset.
constraint: Semantic candidate matching must return required permitted evidence for the actual query distribution.

title: BM25 / lexical
summary: Use literal terms and identifiers as retrieval signals; field configuration and tokenization still matter.
clue: AX-1047 / SKU / policy code may need lexical matching or an exact field lookup.
trap: A semantic similarity score alone can miss a literal identifier.
capability: OpenSearch or another supported lexical search contract for exact terms/identifiers; eligible hybrid can combine semantic signals.
example: Searching a literal SKU should not lose the code because other product descriptions sound similar.
managed: Supported lexical/BM25 search scores configured searchable text fields/terms.
extension: Preserve identifiers and use supported field/tokenization/query settings; evaluate combination with vector signals if eligible.
ownership: Measure exact-ID cases and scope/freshness; lexical relevance is not an access-control guarantee.
constraint: Literal terms and field handling must preserve the identifiers that decide the task.

title: Hybrid
summary: Combine semantic and lexical signals where the selected store/API supports it, then evaluate candidate coverage and relevance.
clue: The question contains both an exact asset ID and a semantic symptom.
trap: Hybrid support and quality vary; it is not universally the best search.
capability: Supported Knowledge Bases/OpenSearch hybrid retrieval joins exact-term and semantic evidence signals.
example: A question includes both a product code and a natural-language symptom; evaluate whether combining literal and semantic signals covers both.
managed: The selected supported retrieval contract combines lexical and vector signals where available.
extension: Configure eligible hybrid behavior and compare it with appropriate alternatives on identical query cases.
ownership: Measure recall/relevance and feature support for this Knowledge Base/store/API; do not assume hybrid is universally superior.
constraint: The selected integration must support the desired combination and improve measured permitted evidence coverage.

title: Candidates
summary: Inspect the permitted evidence actually returned before reranking. Missing candidates may reflect indexing, freshness, filters, or query behavior.
clue: Indexed and authorized source missing here → evaluate candidate recall and query/search.
trap: A reranker cannot score a document absent from its input.
constraint: Required evidence must enter the candidate set before downstream ranking/context can use it.
example: A reranker cannot choose the policy exception if initial search never returned it.
managed: Retrieve or supported store search returns the actual permitted candidate list for the configured query.
extension: Adjust eligible search/query/filter settings and candidate coverage before introducing an ordering stage.
ownership: Inspect record identity, freshness, access, and pre-rerank recall rather than trusting a plausible generated answer.
capability: Knowledge Bases Retrieve isolates candidates from generation; selected search controls addresses coverage.

title: Reranker
summary: Reorder existing candidates for relevance to the question before pruning context. This adds a ranking stage, not a new source-ingestion path.
clue: Correct passage is present but placed below irrelevant candidates.
trap: Reranking cannot restore text never parsed/indexed/retrieved.
constraint: The useful passage must already be in input, and reordering must improve the context actually supplied.
managed: Supported Bedrock/Knowledge Bases reranking reorders supplied candidates for query relevance.
extension: Configure eligible model/result settings and inspect ordering before/after reranking.
ownership: Evaluate relevant passage retention, latency/cost, and the unchanged candidate-input boundary.
capability: Bedrock reranking or Knowledge Bases supported reranking configuration addresses order, not missing index/search content.
example: The correct clause is in candidates but gets dropped below the context cutoff; ordering is the gap to test.

title: Best context
summary: Select authorized relevant evidence within the context budget, preserving qualifications and source references.
clue: Good candidate can still be lost by pruning or truncation before generation.
trap: Top-ranked alone does not mean complete, permitted, or source-supported.
example: Selecting only the short rule while discarding its exception produces misleading context even after good retrieval.
managed: The configured managed retrieval/generation path supplies context under its supported settings.
extension: Use Retrieve plus application selection/pruning or supported parent-context behavior where extra control is required.
ownership: Preserve authorized qualifications, source references, and relevant history within the model input budget.
capability: Knowledge Bases retrieval/parent context and application context assembly chooses which evidence reaches inference.
constraint: Select enough correct permitted evidence to preserve meaning within the supported context limit.

title: System instructions
summary: State task authority, behavior, boundaries, and insufficient-information handling.
clue: Separate governing instructions from untrusted source passages.
trap: A system instruction is not a deterministic access-control boundary.
example: If no authorized passage answers the question, define clarification/fallback behavior instead of inviting the model to invent a policy.
managed: Bedrock supported message/prompt contracts carries governing instructions to the selected model.
extension: Use versioned task rules/examples and supported safety checks around untrusted input.
ownership: Define authority and insufficient-information behavior; keep access/transaction checks deterministic outside model wording.
capability: Prompt Management plus supported inference instructions; Guardrails for eligible safety policies; IAM/backend checks for permission.
constraint: Governing rules must state the task and boundaries without treating retrieved text as instruction authority.

title: Prompt template
summary: Version reusable task instructions, variables, and supported model configuration.
clue: Reproducible prompt releases → Prompt Management.
trap: Saving a version does not mean it passed evaluation.
capability: Prompt Management for reusable/versioned instructions; protected request attribution and release tests for actual invocation.
example: A tested version and a live rendered request can differ because a variable or example changed.
managed: Prompt Management provides supported templates, variables, variants, versions, and model configuration.
extension: Bind supported variables and invoke the evaluated prompt through a compatible API contract.
ownership: Track the rendered payload, release identity, approval/evaluation, and fallback; a saved version is not evidence of live use.
constraint: The rendered version/configuration must match the approved evaluated task requirements.

title: User query
summary: Define the requested task clearly and preserve the question the evidence should answer.
clue: Different label definitions or overlap policies create different classification tasks.
trap: A persona cannot fill in an undefined decision rule.
example: “Choose billing or technical” is incomplete when a case belongs to both and no priority or clarification rule exists.
managed: The inference API accepts the supplied query; it does not define the application’s business labels.
extension: Add explicit task definitions, representative examples, and supported clarification branching.
ownership: Agree expected decisions and missing-information handling, preserving user intent and meaningful identifiers.
capability: Prompt Management for task rules; application/Flows branching for eligible clarification; assertions for expected decisions.
constraint: The requested outcome and ambiguous boundary cases must be defined before measuring model correctness.

title: Retrieved knowledge
summary: Supply selected permitted passages as evidence, keeping their identifiers and source conditions.
clue: A cited passage must actually support the answer claim.
trap: Treat document instructions as untrusted data rather than system authority.
example: The model needs both the current eligibility rule and its exception; an old or incomplete passage is insufficient.
managed: Knowledge Bases supplies supported retrieved evidence under its configured search/access contract.
extension: Use Retrieve/context assembly or compatible managed generation settings to include the required permitted passages.
ownership: Verify freshness, entitlement, qualifications, source identity, and what actually reaches the model.
capability: Knowledge Bases Retrieve/RetrieveAndGenerate for eligible evidence supply; application checks for the needed facts and source support.
constraint: Supply the current authorized facts and qualifiers required by this question.

title: Conversation context
summary: Supply relevant permitted history and authoritative state explicitly; trim within the context budget.
clue: Converse accepts messages; the application owns the history it sends.
trap: An inference call is not automatically a persistent conversation store.
example: A follow-up about “that device” needs its earlier ID included in relevant scoped history or authoritative state.
managed: Converse/ConverseStream receives supported message history supplied by the application.
extension: Select relevant turns and application state explicitly, trimming within the supported context budget.
ownership: Persist authoritative facts, enforce session/tenant scope, and verify required details survive history trimming.
capability: Converse messages for current context; appropriate application state storage such as DynamoDB for durable scoped facts.
constraint: Preserve enough relevant authorized history/state to answer the current task within the model budget.

title: Amazon Bedrock
summary: Use eligible managed foundation models, inference APIs, customization, and supporting GenAI capabilities without choosing endpoint GPU fleets.
clue: Managed FM-centric application integration fits without infrastructure selection.
trap: Bedrock supports eligible customization; “custom weights” alone does not require SageMaker.
capability: Bedrock Converse/model APIs and supported Knowledge Bases/Guardrails/customization features for their respective responsibilities.
example: Use an eligible managed model without designing a GPU endpoint fleet, while still evaluating the actual task and feature contract.
managed: Bedrock provides supported FM inference infrastructure and eligible customization/import/application capabilities.
extension: Configure supported prompts, tools, retrieval, safety, and adaptation around eligible model/API features.
ownership: Own model/task fit, inputs/scope, release checks, and business outcomes; managed inference is not automatic correctness.
constraint: The chosen model/feature/Region/API must meet task, processing, and serving requirements.

title: SageMaker AI
summary: Choose deeper ML training, serving-container, instance, endpoint, and lifecycle controls where they are decisive.
clue: GPU family + serving container + endpoint autoscaling requirements.
trap: More control adds ownership; do not choose it merely because a prompt or chunker is custom.
managed: SageMaker AI supplies managed jobs/endpoints and supported lifecycle components with configurable ML/hosting choices.
ownership: Own the implementation/configuration, capacity economics, artifact compatibility, evaluation, and deployment/rollback.
capability: SageMaker endpoints/jobs/pipelines/eligible registry components when their deeper control is required; custom weights alone do not rule out Bedrock.
example: A required custom serving container, GPU instance choice, or endpoint scaling policy calls for deeper hosting control.
extension: Provide compatible model/container/artifact and endpoint settings, or use supported adapter inference components where eligible.
constraint: Take deeper training/hosting control only where a hard requirement justifies its configuration and operations.

title: Synchronous
summary: The caller waits for one complete bounded response.
clue: Short complete answer needed before proceeding.
trap: A larger timeout does not turn the path into durable background work.
capability: Converse or compatible InvokeModel for supported bounded inference; application/API delivery and outcome validation.
example: A user waits for one bounded complete answer; its response timeout must fit the whole request path.
managed: Supported Bedrock synchronous inference produces the complete operation result.
extension: Use a compatible API/application integration and validate the delivered task result.
ownership: Own timeout/retry uncertainty, authorization, and whether this work fits a bounded waiting caller.
constraint: The complete request must fit the caller’s waiting/time contract and return a valid result.

title: Streaming / ConverseStream
summary: Expose incremental generated output while the caller stays connected; every transport hop must preserve streaming.
clue: Need earlier visible tokens while the user waits.
trap: Streaming does not imply background completion or lower total inference cost.
capability: Bedrock streaming plus supported end-to-end transport; verify each hop and model/API support.
example: The first token is useful only if the adapter/API/proxy/client forwards it rather than buffering until completion.
managed: ConverseStream or another supported Bedrock operation exposes incremental model output.
extension: Implement a supported streaming transport/client path and compatible event decoding.
ownership: Handle buffering, disconnects, partial failure, safe output, and resource cleanup without assuming a resumed model stream.
constraint: The caller remains connected and receives incremental output under safe delivery/error handling.

title: Asynchronous
summary: Return durable acceptance/job identity and finish later with persisted status/results and failure handling.
clue: Caller can leave; accepted work must survive transient worker failures.
trap: Acknowledged is not completed, and a queue does not by itself enforce token rate.
capability: SQS/Step Functions plus application job state; SageMaker Asynchronous Inference where its hosting/job contract fits.
example: Return a job ID quickly, then persist real pending/completed/failed state so the caller can leave and return later.
managed: Queues/workflows and compatible job services supply their configured background execution contracts.
extension: Compose durable application workers, results/status, polling or callbacks, and supported model work.
ownership: Own acceptance versus completion, authorization, retries/idempotency, reconciliation, and durable result retention.
constraint: Accepted work must survive the caller leaving and expose truthful recoverable completion state.

title: Batch
summary: Process a supported offline dataset as a managed inference job and reconcile record-level results.
clue: Many offline requests; no immediate live answer is needed.
trap: Batch support, input format, economics, and completion semantics depend on the model/Region contract.
capability: Bedrock batch inference or SageMaker Batch Transform according to the dataset/hosting requirement; not interactive token delivery.
example: A known offline S3 dataset should be reconciled by record after the eligible inference job finishes.
managed: Supported Bedrock batch inference processes an eligible dataset/job contract; SageMaker Batch Transform fits appropriate custom-hosted batch work.
extension: Prepare supported records and correlate/reconcile output and failure records.
ownership: Check model/Region support, completion objectives, job failures, permissions, and measured economics.
constraint: Use a supported offline job and verify record-level completion under the task deadline.

title: Select
summary: Compare supported model capability, modalities, context limits, quality, safety, latency, cost, and deployment requirements.
clue: Choose with representative tasks and a held-out baseline.
trap: A public benchmark rank does not establish fit for this workload.
example: Compare two supported candidates on the same real task cases; a stronger public benchmark may not help your required modality, rare IDs, or latency budget.
managed: Bedrock exposes eligible models through supported inference APIs; evaluation operations provide supported measurement approaches. SageMaker can host compatible candidates where deeper control is needed.
extension: Use a representative held-out dataset and consistent rubric/settings; route among evaluated eligible models where the requirements call for it.
ownership: Own the acceptance criteria, workload/cohort coverage, fair comparison, and support checks. Do not substitute model size or reputation for measured task fit.
capability: Bedrock inference/evaluation or compatible SageMaker hosting supports model comparison. AppConfig plus application routing can change approved model/cohort selection under its deployment/polling contract.
constraint: The candidate must meet task/modality, context/output, safety, latency/cost, Region/API, and deployment requirements.

comparison.title: Bedrock or SageMaker AI: which responsibility do you need to control?
comparison.note: Choose a model that passes representative task, modality, quality, safety, latency, cost, and Region/API requirements. Measure cost per successful task.
comparison.techniqueNote: Both services are managed. Bedrock supports customization; SageMaker adds control where needed. Eligible SageMaker-trained models can be imported into Bedrock—training and serving choices can differ.

title: Choose context or model changes
summary: Change instructions, evidence, or weights according to the observed deficiency; these approaches can combine. Prompt → RAG → weights: escalate only for an unmet need. This is an application decision, separate from the model-only lifecycle.
clue: Missing current facts differs from unstable instructions or stable style needs. Change instructions, evidence, or weights deliberately; evaluate each against a held-out baseline.
trap: RAG is not fine-tuning and neither is required for every model change.
extension: Improve task instructions/examples, add supported RAG, or test eligible adaptation according to the measured gap.
example: A format gap, a current-fact gap, and a stable learned-behavior gap require different experiments and may coexist.
managed: Prompt Management, Knowledge Bases, and eligible Bedrock/SageMaker customization provide different instruction, evidence, and weight capabilities.
ownership: Define the requirement, fair baseline, data/evaluation, and release controls for each change.
capability: Prompt → task/format; RAG → current permitted evidence; eligible customization → evaluated stable behavior/domain need.
constraint: Change the layer whose missing responsibility explains the observed defect, accepting custom ownership only where required.

title: Model customization / training (optional)
summary: Change the model only for an evaluated need. Compare any adapted candidate with the unchanged baseline, then evaluate before deployment. An unchanged selected model can also proceed directly to evaluation.
constraint: Change weights only for a measured requirement with suitable data, supported method, demonstrated benefit, and a compatible release path.
managed: Eligible Bedrock customization/distillation/import features or SageMaker jobs/endpoints supply supported adaptation and deployment operations. Availability depends on model/method/Region/serving contract.
extension: Choose labeled-data tuning, supported unlabeled domain adaptation, or eligible teacher/student distillation for the measured requirement. LoRA changes adapter weights within a compatible tuning/serving setup.
ownership: Own approved examples, independent evaluation, artifact compatibility, approval, deployment, and rollback. A trained artifact is not proof that the live application uses it or that its behavior improved.
capability: Bedrock eligible customization/import/distillation or SageMaker model/adapter workflows addresses weight-level needs. Prompt Management and Knowledge Bases addresses separate instruction/evidence gaps.
clue: Stable behavior → fine-tuning; supported domain-text adaptation → continued pre-training; smaller student → distillation.
trap: RAG is not fine-tuning and neither is required for every model change.
example: If clear instructions and correct evidence still fail a stable behavior requirement, test eligible adaptation and compare it with the unchanged baseline.

comparison.title: Which kind of model change fits?
comparison.note: Compare held-out quality and full lifecycle cost. Smaller artifacts do not guarantee cheaper serving; changing weights does not create a live source lookup.
comparison.techniqueNote: LoRA = weight-update technique. DAPT = domain-focused continued pre-training. Distillation = teacher-to-student transfer; it can use SFT. Check model/method/runtime support.

title: Prompt engineering
summary: Clarify task, decision rules, examples, and supported output constraints before adding weight changes.
clue: Policy ambiguity or a missing few-shot boundary.
trap: A valid schema or low temperature cannot supply a missing fact.
capability: Prompt Management plus Converse/model APIs; schema validation and task assertions checks different requirements.
example: Define how overlapping categories should be handled, then test examples before assuming the model needs weight changes.
managed: Prompt Management versions reusable instructions/examples; the supported inference contract carries the rendered context.
extension: Add task rules, examples, relevant evidence, and supported output constraints.
ownership: Own label meanings, semantic/business assertions, untrusted-data separation, and prompt regression gates.
constraint: The prompt must express a clear task with testable expected outputs and appropriate evidence.

title: RAG
summary: Retrieve current private evidence into context rather than relying on model weights to track updates.
clue: Frequently changing source facts with attribution.
trap: RAG still needs ingestion freshness, authorization, retrieval quality, and faithful context use.
capability: Knowledge Bases Retrieve/RetrieveAndGenerate with a supported store; Lambda transformation extends ingestion, supported reranking addresses candidate order.
example: A policy changed after training; retrieve its current permitted rule and exception instead of assuming weights track every update.
managed: Knowledge Bases coordinates supported source ingestion and retrieval/generation with the selected backing contract.
extension: Use supported ingestion/filter/reranking extensions or compose Retrieve/context assembly for the specific gap.
ownership: Own freshness, caller entitlement, source meaning, candidate/answer evaluation, and unsupported policy.
constraint: Current authorized evidence must reach context and actually support the requested answer.

title: Fine-tuning
